inputs.question: In low- and middle-income countries, do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work, and which kinds work best?
inputs.scope:
Covers: Interventions delivered in low- and middle-income countries that aim to improve educational outcomes (enrolment, attendance, retention, progression, learning or achievement) for children and young people with any type of disability. The question covers whether these programmes work at all and how the main programme types compare on effectiveness and on the certainty of that evidence.
Out of scope:
- Effectiveness of disability-inclusive education programmes in high-income countries (Different school systems, resources and evidence base. The question is explicitly limited to LMICs.)
- Education interventions for all children that do not target or report outcomes for children with disabilities (General education evidence cannot show effects specific to children with disabilities.)
- Health, functional or rehabilitation outcomes (e.g. mobility, vision correction itself) where no education outcome is measured (The question is about education results, not clinical or functional gains.)
- Whether inclusive or segregated schooling is the right policy as a matter of rights or law (e.g. under the UN CRPD) (That is a normative and legal question, not an empirical one about programme effects.)
- Detailed cost-effectiveness or budget comparisons between programmes (These need costing data beyond effectiveness evidence. Costs may be noted where reviews report them, but they will not be the basis of the verdict.)
- Prevalence of disability or the size of the education gap for children with disabilities (Describing the problem is separate from whether interventions fix it.)

inputs.question: In low- and middle-income countries, do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work, and which kinds work best?
inputs.scope:
Covers: Interventions delivered in low- and middle-income countries that aim to improve educational outcomes (enrolment, attendance, retention, progression, learning or achievement) for children and young people with any type of disability. The question covers whether these programmes work at all and how the main programme types compare on effectiveness and on the certainty of that evidence.
Out of scope:
- Effectiveness of disability-inclusive education programmes in high-income countries (Different school systems, resources and evidence base. The question is explicitly limited to LMICs.)
- Education interventions for all children that do not target or report outcomes for children with disabilities (General education evidence cannot show effects specific to children with disabilities.)
- Health, functional or rehabilitation outcomes (e.g. mobility, vision correction itself) where no education outcome is measured (The question is about education results, not clinical or functional gains.)
- Whether inclusive or segregated schooling is the right policy as a matter of rights or law (e.g. under the UN CRPD) (That is a normative and legal question, not an empirical one about programme effects.)
- Detailed cost-effectiveness or budget comparisons between programmes (These need costing data beyond effectiveness evidence. Costs may be noted where reviews report them, but they will not be the basis of the verdict.)
- Prevalence of disability or the size of the education gap for children with disabilities (Describing the problem is separate from whether interventions fix it.)
